# BLO-32424 — guard the Secret adoption write against the reaper/writer races

Changed files:

- `src/server/execute.ts` — in `createOrAdoptRunSecret`, the adoption write is now
  a merge `patchNamespacedSecret` rather than `replaceNamespacedSecret`, and its
  404 and 409 responses route back through the bounded retry loop's existing
  `continue` instead of escaping the `catch (err)` block. The three
  `ownerReference` attaches now state their JSON Patch `Content-Type` explicitly.
- `src/server/secret-adopt.test.ts`, `src/server/execute.test.ts` — coverage for
  both new paths, the unchanged retry budget, and the fail-closed case.

## Why

The adoption write was the last create-or-write in that function outside a
guard, and it sits *inside* the `catch` block — so a 404 (the reaper freed the
name between our read and the write) or a 409 (stale `resourceVersion` under a
concurrent writer) escaped the bounded `for` loop entirely, with no second pass
and no adoption, surfacing as the same `k8s_*_secret_create_failed` that
[BLO-31665](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-31665) added the
adoption path to prevent. Detecting the conflict is only half the job if
detection still kills the run. Both now re-enter the loop: 404 means the name is
free, so re-create; 409 means re-read and retry. No third code path and no new
retry budget — the loop's existing bound governs both, so a later change cannot
quietly raise it. Any other error still fails closed with its original identity,
and `resourceVersion` is still carried, so optimistic concurrency is preserved
rather than dropped to dodge the conflict.

## On the verb, and what this change is *not*

A replace is a PUT, i.e. the `update` verb, which
`deploy/helm/paperclip/templates/role.yaml` did not grant — so before that Role
changed, the adoption path returned 403 on every collision, deterministically,
and never reached the races it was added to survive. **That 403 is already
closed by a different route:**
[#1837](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1837) merged
2026-09-16T06:42Z and added `update` to the Role; the live grant is confirmed by
SSAR against `system:serviceaccount:paperclip:paperclip` in ns `paperclip`
(`secrets:update` allowed, attributed to RoleBinding
`paperclip-k8s-adapters/paperclip`). This change is therefore **not** the remedy
for a still-bleeding 403 — it is the narrower one. `patch` was already granted
before #1837, so the adopt path needs no widened verb at all: *this adapter* is
not what holds `update` open.

Whether that grant is now retirable outright is a separate question and is
**not** settled here. The sandbox-provider plugin's PUT at
`packages/plugins/sandbox-providers/kubernetes/src/secret-manager.ts` runs under
the same service account but in a *tenant* namespace the release-namespace Role
never covered, so it neither justifies nor blocks retirement. Tracked as
[BLO-34510](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-34510), which carries
the pin-bump guard that has to land with any removal; the justification block in
`deploy/helm/paperclip/templates/role.yaml` records what was measured. The
404/409 retry routing is independent of the verb question and is the part
BLO-32424 was actually filed for.

## The explicit JSON Patch Content-Type

From an Ally review suggestion on
[#1873](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1873). The three
`ownerReference` attaches send JSON Patch arrays and inherited the client's
default, which `ObjectSerializer.getPreferredMediaType` resolves to the *first*
accepted media type — so a client-version bump that reordered that list would
break all three with no diff in this repo. Behaviour-preserving. Only two of the
three are reachable at runtime in `execute.test.ts` (it pins
`PAPERCLIP_SHARED_MCP_BASELINE_PATH` to `""`, so `mcpConfigSecret` is never
staged), so the third is covered by a static count pin in the BLO-33894 style;
all three were mutation-tested to confirm each reverts red on its own.

No upstream change: this is Paperclip-local code under `src/server/`, not a
carried patch against an upstream adapter release.
